steps.title: Breastfeeding

steps.title: Bottle feeding
steps.body: Log expressed milk, formula or a mix of both. Add the amount you recorded, all in the same place.

steps.title: Pumping
steps.body: Time a pumping session and add a volume if you have one. Your expressed-milk balance updates from the entries you record.

steps.title: Combined feeds
steps.body: A breastfeed followed by a bottle top-up? Save them together as one feed, with both parts easy to find.

faqs.question: Is Breastfeeding Tracker free?
faqs.answer: The app is free to download and start using. An optional one-time Lifetime Unlock adds full history, filters, insights, PDF export, all themes and an ad-free experience. There is no subscription.

faqs.question: Can I track breastfeeding, bottles and pumping?
faqs.answer: Yes. Record breastfeeding, bottle feeds and pumping in the same timeline. Combined feeds keep a breastfeed and a bottle top-up together in one entry. Bottles can include expressed milk, formula or a mix.

faqs.question: What if I forget to start the timer?
faqs.answer: Move the recorded start time back while a timer is running, or add a completed feed later. You can also edit or delete entries from your history.

faqs.question: Does Apple Watch work without my phone nearby?
faqs.answer: Yes. Start and stop breastfeeding or pumping timers from your wrist. Completed sessions sync back to your iPhone when your devices reconnect.

faqs.question: Do I need to create an account?
faqs.answer: No app account is required. Open the app and start tracking.

faqs.question: Can I share my feeding history?
faqs.answer: With Lifetime Unlock, export selected feeds as a PDF and choose where to save or share it. The PDF contains the details you recorded, which can be useful for a conversation with a midwife or feeding-support professional.

faqs.question: Does the app tell me if my baby is getting enough milk?
faqs.answer: No. The app records what you enter and offers informational summaries. It does not measure milk intake from breastfeeding, assess milk supply or provide medical advice. Speak to your midwife, health visitor or feeding-support professional if you have concerns.
